title: Unequal Opportunities: Examining the Bias in Geographical Recommendations by Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Assessing the over- and under-representation of specific U.S. cities and towns in LLM recommendations using inequality metrics like the concentration ratio and the Theil index to evaluate distributional inequality.

Comparing financial and educational attributes (e.g., poverty, unemployment rate, median rent, home value, college education) of LLM-recommended cities against external U.S. city databases using skewness and t-tests.

Analyzing the skewness and distributional differences of specific racial demographics (e.g., Black, Native, Hispanic, Pacific Islander, Asian, White populations) in LLM-recommended cities compared to real-world census data.
Assessing the distribution of the female population in LLM-recommended locations using statistical skewness across relocation, business, and tourism queries.
Evaluating the percentage of the disabled population in cities recommended by LLMs against the U.S. city database distributions to identify under-representation.
Evaluating the age demographics (e.g., median age, populations over 65, populations under 19) of the recommended cities to identify systematic preferences for younger or older populations.
